claims.text: Potassium chloride ER (Klor-Con) label: K < 2.5 mEq/L: use IV K, not PO.
claims.quote: If serum potassium concentration is less than 2.5 mEq/L, use intravenous potassium instead of oral supplementation.

claims.text: Monitor K and adjust; recheck periodically during maintenance.
claims.quote: Monitor serum potassium and adjust dosages accordingly. Monitor serum potassium periodically during maintenance therapy to ensure potassium remains in desired range.

claims.text: Take w meals and a glass of water, ⍉ on an empty stomach (gastric irritation); swallow whole (⍉ crush, chew or suck).
claims.quote: Take KLOR-CON with meals and with a glass of water or other liquid. Do not take KLOR-CON on an empty stomach because of its potential for gastric irritation [see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)] . Swallow tablets whole without crushing, chewing or sucking.

claims.text: Doses > 40 mEq/day: divide so ≤ 40 mEq per dose.
claims.quote: Dosages greater than 40 mEq per day should be divided such that no more than 40 mEq is given in a single dose.

claims.text: Hypokalemia: typically 40 to 100 mEq/day; maintenance or prophylaxis: typically 20 mEq/day.
claims.quote: Treatment of Hypokalemia:Typical dose range is 40 to 100 mEq per day. Maintenance or Prophylaxis:Typical dose range is 20 mEq per day.
Use with triamterene or amiloride can produce severe hyperkalemia. Concomitant use is contraindicated

claims.text: Solid forms can cause ulcerative or stenotic GI lesions; consider liquid K in dysphagia or severe GI motility disorders.
claims.quote: Solid oral dosage forms of potassium chloride can produce ulcerative and/or stenotic lesions of the gastrointestinal tract, particularly if the drug maintains contact with the gastrointestinal mucosa for prolonged periods. Consider the use of liquid potassium in patients with dysphagia, swallowing disorders, or severe gastrointestinal motility disorders.

claims.text: Severe vomiting, abd pain, distention or GI bleeding: stop and consider ulceration, obstruction or perforation.
claims.quote: If severe vomiting, abdominal pain, distention, or gastrointestinal bleeding occurs, discontinue KLOR-CON extended-release tablets and consider possibility of ulceration, obstruction or perforation.

claims.text: RAAS inhibitors (ACEi, ARB, spironolactone, eplerenone, aliskiren): closely monitor K;
claims.quote: Drugs that inhibit the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) including angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs), spironolactone, eplerenone, or aliskiren produce potassium retention by inhibiting aldosterone production. Closely monitor potassium in patients on concomitant RAAS inhibitors.
Closely monitor potassium in patients on concomitant NSAIDs.
